rows.tent: SubQ's subq-snap-1.1, in public preview, through its Decisions API, which also takes images. Its option probabilities arrive as 32-bit floats, so they sum to 1 only within 32-bit rounding. Its probability check used an experimental 32-bit rule of ours. For this model only, the check before its runs accepted a sum within one 32-bit epsilon (2^-23) per option when every value is an exact 32-bit float, instead of 7 decimal places; this is our tolerance, not an error bound SubQ states. The values are stored as SubQ returned them. It was paused twice while the approval of its probability check was confirmed, for 12 minutes and then for 3 hours 24 minutes, and resumed from its stored answers. The two requests in flight count those pauses in their times (706 and 12,236 seconds; the first after one retry, when SubQ had closed the connection), so the run's total request time and questions per minute include them. Without them, its median request time stays 0.378 s and its 90th percentile moves from 0.388 s to 0.387 s.

rows.tent: SubQ's subq-snap-1.1, in public preview, through its Decisions API, which also takes images. Its option probabilities arrive as 32-bit floats, so they sum to 1 only within 32-bit rounding. Its probability check used an experimental 32-bit rule of ours. For this model only, the check before its runs accepted a sum within one 32-bit epsilon (2^-23) per option when every value is an exact 32-bit float, instead of 7 decimal places; this is our tolerance, not an error bound SubQ states. The values are stored as SubQ returned them. It was paused twice while the approval of its probability check was confirmed, for 12 minutes and then for 3 hours 24 minutes, and resumed from its stored answers. The two requests in flight count those pauses in their times (706 and 12,236 seconds; the first after one retry, when SubQ had closed the connection), so the run's total request time and questions per minute include them. Without them, its median request time stays 0.378 s and its 90th percentile moves from 0.388 s to 0.387 s.

rows.tent: SubQ's subq-snap-1.1, in public preview, through its Decisions API, which also takes images. Its option probabilities arrive as 32-bit floats, so they sum to 1 only within 32-bit rounding. Its probability check used an experimental 32-bit rule of ours. For this model only, the check before its runs accepted a sum within one 32-bit epsilon (2^-23) per option when every value is an exact 32-bit float, instead of 7 decimal places; this is our tolerance, not an error bound SubQ states. The values are stored as SubQ returned them. It was paused twice while the approval of its probability check was confirmed, for 12 minutes and then for 3 hours 24 minutes, and resumed from its stored answers. The two requests in flight count those pauses in their times (706 and 12,236 seconds; the first after one retry, when SubQ had closed the connection), so the run's total request time and questions per minute include them. Without them, its median request time stays 0.378 s and its 90th percentile moves from 0.388 s to 0.387 s.

rows.normLabel: 0 = guessing among 5 options, 100 = every answer right
rows.method: vLLM, the maker's image, on our GPU (logic's load, RTX PRO 6000); reasoning effort 0.9, temperature 0, seed 0; one question per request, answer line 'ANSWER: X'
rows.limit: The science bench: hard maths and physics questions, asked in English (the Turkish originals are kept as separate tables at the end of the list). University maths & physics: 50 problems (25 maths, 25 physics) from university textbooks and exams, every given number changed and the answer recomputed by code, five options of which four are typical mistakes. High-school maths: 32 questions from the first stage of a 2026 national high-school maths olympiad, with its official answer key; public since May 2026, so a model trained on later data may have seen them. Broken questions: the 50 university problems mixed with 42 copies in which one given number was changed so that none of the five options is right (checked by code), with a sixth option F 'the question is flawed'; right means F on a broken copy and the right option on an intact one. Exact answers: the same 50 university problems with no options; the model writes the number, right when within 0.1% of the code's value; a reply that is not a number counts wrong. Latency and cost: on our GPU, median seconds per problem with the requests in flight shown, and GPU time from start to last answer × $2.49 per GPU-hour per 1,000 problems; subscription routes, the tokens they reported at the maker's API list price, nothing billed. Decision and small models were asked one question per request; the subscription models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, MAI) 16 per request through their own tools, marked batched where it matters. The English text was translated from the Turkish originals by Gemini 4 Neon and checked again by GPT-6.2 Astra, every number compared by code. The questions are not published; right or wrong per problem for every run is in https://zekiworks.github.io/analysis/science/answers.json, for paired tests. A reply without a readable letter counts wrong.

rows.limit: The science bench: hard maths and physics questions, asked in English (the Turkish originals are kept as separate tables at the end of the list). University maths & physics: 50 problems (25 maths, 25 physics) from university textbooks and exams, every given number changed and the answer recomputed by code, five options of which four are typical mistakes. High-school maths: 32 questions from the first stage of a 2026 national high-school maths olympiad, with its official answer key; public since May 2026, so a model trained on later data may have seen them. Broken questions: the 50 university problems mixed with 42 copies in which one given number was changed so that none of the five options is right (checked by code), with a sixth option F 'the question is flawed'; right means F on a broken copy and the right option on an intact one. Exact answers: the same 50 university problems with no options; the model writes the number, right when within 0.1% of the code's value; a reply that is not a number counts wrong. Latency and cost: on our GPU, median seconds per problem with the requests in flight shown, and GPU time from start to last answer × $2.49 per GPU-hour per 1,000 problems; subscription routes, the tokens they reported at the maker's API list price, nothing billed. Decision and small models were asked one question per request; the subscription models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, MAI) 16 per request through their own tools, marked batched where it matters. The English text was translated from the Turkish originals by Gemini 4 Neon and checked again by GPT-6.2 Astra, every number compared by code. The questions are not published; right or wrong per problem for every run is in https://zekiworks.github.io/analysis/science/answers.json, for paired tests. A reply without a readable letter counts wrong.
rows.costBasis: GPU time from the run's start to its last answer × $2.49 per GPU-hour ÷ problems (not an invoice)

rows.method: on our GPU (compactor's load, RTX PRO 6000, shared with other runs), Liquid's model code behind our server; one question per request
rows.limit: The science bench: hard maths and physics questions, asked in English (the Turkish originals are kept as separate tables at the end of the list). University maths & physics: 50 problems (25 maths, 25 physics) from university textbooks and exams, every given number changed and the answer recomputed by code, five options of which four are typical mistakes. High-school maths: 32 questions from the first stage of a 2026 national high-school maths olympiad, with its official answer key; public since May 2026, so a model trained on later data may have seen them. Broken questions: the 50 university problems mixed with 42 copies in which one given number was changed so that none of the five options is right (checked by code), with a sixth option F 'the question is flawed'; right means F on a broken copy and the right option on an intact one. Exact answers: the same 50 university problems with no options; the model writes the number, right when within 0.1% of the code's value; a reply that is not a number counts wrong. Latency and cost: on our GPU, median seconds per problem with the requests in flight shown, and GPU time from start to last answer × $2.49 per GPU-hour per 1,000 problems; subscription routes, the tokens they reported at the maker's API list price, nothing billed. Decision and small models were asked one question per request; the subscription models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, MAI) 16 per request through their own tools, marked batched where it matters. The English text was translated from the Turkish originals by Gemini 4 Neon and checked again by GPT-6.2 Astra, every number compared by code. The questions are not published; right or wrong per problem for every run is in https://zekiworks.github.io/analysis/science/answers.json, for paired tests. A reply without a readable letter counts wrong.
rows.costBasis: GPU time from the run's start to its last answer × $2.49 per GPU-hour ÷ problems (not an invoice); card shared with other benches' runs, so not this run's alone

rows.limit: The science bench: hard maths and physics questions, asked in English (the Turkish originals are kept as separate tables at the end of the list). rows.method: vLLM, the maker's image, on our GPU (logic's load, RTX PRO 6000); reasoning effort 0.9, temperature 0, seed 0; one question per request, answer line 'ANSWER: X'
rows.limit: The science bench: hard maths and physics questions, asked in English (the Turkish originals are kept as separate tables at the end of the list). University maths & physics: 50 problems (25 maths, 25 physics) from university textbooks and exams, every given number changed and the answer recomputed by code, five options of which four are typical mistakes. High-school maths: 32 questions from the first stage of a 2026 national high-school maths olympiad, with its official answer key; public since May 2026, so a model trained on later data may have seen them. Broken questions: the 50 university problems mixed with 42 copies in which one given number was changed so that none of the five options is right (checked by code), with a sixth option F 'the question is flawed'; right means F on a broken copy and the right option on an intact one. Exact answers: the same 50 university problems with no options; the model writes the number, right when within 0.1% of the code's value; a reply that is not a number counts wrong. Latency and cost: on our GPU, median seconds per problem with the requests in flight shown, and GPU time from start to last answer × $2.49 per GPU-hour per 1,000 problems; subscription routes, the tokens they reported at the maker's API list price, nothing billed. Decision and small models were asked one question per request; the subscription models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, MAI) 16 per request through their own tools, marked batched where it matters. The English text was translated from the Turkish originals by Gemini 4 Neon and checked again by GPT-6.2 Astra, every number compared by code. The questions are not published; right or wrong per problem for every run is in https://zekiworks.github.io/analysis/science/answers.json, for paired tests. A reply without a readable letter counts wrong.

High-school maths: 32 questions from the first stage of a 2026 national high-school maths olympiad, with its official answer key; public since May 2026, so a model trained on later data may have seen them. Broken questions: the 50 university problems mixed with 42 copies in which one given number was changed so that none of the five options is right (checked by code), with a sixth option F 'the question is flawed'; right means F on a broken copy and the right option on an intact one. Decision and small models were asked one question per request; the subscription models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, MAI) 16 per request through their own tools, marked batched where it matters. The English text was translated from the Turkish originals by Gemini 4 Neon and checked again by GPT-6.2 Astra, every number compared by code. The questions are not published; right or wrong per problem for every run is in https://zekiworks.github.io/analysis/science/answers.json, for paired tests. A reply without a readable letter counts wrong.
rows.costBasis: GPU time from the run's start to its last answer × $2.49 per GPU-hour ÷ problems (not an invoice)

High-school maths: 32 questions from the first stage of a 2026 national high-school maths olympiad, with its official answer key; public since May 2026, so a model trained on later data may have seen them. Broken questions: the 50 university problems mixed with 42 copies in which one given number was changed so that none of the five options is right (checked by code), with a sixth option F 'the question is flawed'; right means F on a broken copy and the right option on an intact one. Exact answers: the same 50 university problems with no options; the model writes the number, right when within 0.1% of the code's value; a reply that is not a number counts wrong. Latency and cost: on our GPU, median seconds per problem with the requests in flight shown, and GPU time from start to last answer × $2.49 per GPU-hour per 1,000 problems; subscription routes, the tokens they reported at the maker's API list price, nothing billed. Decision and small models were asked one question per request; the subscription models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, MAI) 16 per request through their own tools, marked batched where it matters. The English text was translated from the Turkish originals by Gemini 4 Neon and checked again by GPT-6.2 Astra, every number compared by code. The questions are not published; right or wrong per problem for every run is in https://zekiworks.github.io/analysis/science/answers.json, for paired tests. A reply without a readable letter counts wrong.

rows.limit: The science bench: hard maths and physics questions, asked in English (the Turkish originals are kept as separate tables at the end of the list). High-school maths: 32 questions from the first stage of a 2026 national high-school maths olympiad, with its official answer key; public since May 2026, so a model trained on later data may have seen them. Broken questions: the 50 university problems mixed with 42 copies in which one given number was changed so that none of the five options is right (checked by code), with a sixth option F 'the question is flawed'; right means F on a broken copy and the right option on an intact one. Exact answers: the same 50 university problems with no options; the model writes the number, right when within 0.1% of the code's value; a reply that is not a number counts wrong. Latency and cost: on our GPU, median seconds per problem with the requests in flight shown, and GPU time from start to last answer × $2.49 per GPU-hour per 1,000 problems; subscription routes, the tokens they reported at the maker's API list price, nothing billed. Decision and small models were asked one question per request; the subscription models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, MAI) 16 per request through their own tools, marked batched where it matters. The English text was translated from the Turkish originals by Gemini 4 Neon and checked again by GPT-6.2 Astra, every number compared by code. The questions are not published; right or wrong per problem for every run is in https://zekiworks.github.io/analysis/science/answers.json, for paired tests. A reply without a readable letter counts wrong.

Broken questions: the 50 university problems mixed with 42 copies in which one given number was changed so that none of the five options is right (checked by code), with a sixth option F 'the question is flawed'; right means F on a broken copy and the right option on an intact one. Decision and small models were asked one question per request; the subscription models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, MAI) 16 per request through their own tools, marked batched where it matters. The English text was translated from the Turkish originals by Gemini 4 Neon and checked again by GPT-6.2 Astra, every number compared by code. University maths & physics: 50 problems (25 maths, 25 physics) from university textbooks and exams, every given number changed and the answer recomputed by code, five options of which four are typical mistakes. High-school maths: 32 questions from the first stage of a 2026 national high-school maths olympiad, with its official answer key; public since May 2026, so a model trained on later data may have seen them. Broken questions: the 50 university problems mixed with 42 copies in which one given number was changed so that none of the five options is right (checked by code), with a sixth option F 'the question is flawed'; right means F on a broken copy and the right option on an intact one. Exact answers: the same 50 university problems with no options; the model writes the number, right when within 0.1% of the code's value; a reply that is not a number counts wrong. Latency and cost: on our GPU, median seconds per problem with the requests in flight shown, and GPU time from start to last answer × $2.49 per GPU-hour per 1,000 problems; subscription routes, the tokens they reported at the maker's API list price, nothing billed. Decision and small models were asked one question per request; the subscription models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, MAI) 16 per request through their own tools, marked batched where it matters. The English text was translated from the Turkish originals by Gemini 4 Neon and checked again by GPT-6.2 Astra, every number compared by code. The questions are not published; right or wrong per problem for every run is in https://zekiworks.github.io/analysis/science/answers.json, for paired tests. A reply without a readable letter counts wrong.
rows.costBasis: GPU time from the run's start to its last answer × $2.49 per GPU-hour ÷ problems (not an invoice)

High-school maths: 32 questions from the first stage of a 2026 national high-school maths olympiad, with its official answer key; public since May 2026, so a model trained on later data may have seen them. Broken questions: the 50 university problems mixed with 42 copies in which one given number was changed so that none of the five options is right (checked by code), with a sixth option F 'the question is flawed'; right means F on a broken copy and the right option on an intact one. Exact answers: the same 50 university problems with no options; the model writes the number, right when within 0.1% of the code's value; a reply that is not a number counts wrong. Latency and cost: on our GPU, median seconds per problem with the requests in flight shown, and GPU time from start to last answer × $2.49 per GPU-hour per 1,000 problems; subscription routes, the tokens they reported at the maker's API list price, nothing billed. Decision and small models were asked one question per request; the subscription models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, MAI) 16 per request through their own tools, marked batched where it matters. The English text was translated from the Turkish originals by Gemini 4 Neon and checked again by GPT-6.2 Astra, every number compared by code. The questions are not published; right or wrong per problem for every run is in https://zekiworks.github.io/analysis/science/answers.json, for paired tests. A reply without a readable letter counts wrong.
rows.costBasis: GPU time from the run's start to its last answer × $2.49 per GPU-hour ÷ problems (not an invoice)

rows.limit: The science bench: hard maths and physics questions, asked in English (the Turkish originals are kept as separate tables at the end of the list). University maths & physics: 50 problems (25 maths, 25 physics) from university textbooks and exams, every given number changed and the answer recomputed by code, five options of which four are typical mistakes. High-school maths: 32 questions from the first stage of a 2026 national high-school maths olympiad, with its official answer key; public since May 2026, so a model trained on later data may have seen them. Broken questions: the 50 university problems mixed with 42 copies in which one given number was changed so that none of the five options is right (checked by code), with a sixth option F 'the question is flawed'; right means F on a broken copy and the right option on an intact one. Exact answers: the same 50 university problems with no options; the model writes the number, right when within 0.1% of the code's value; a reply that is not a number counts wrong. Latency and cost: on our GPU, median seconds per problem with the requests in flight shown, and GPU time from start to last answer × $2.49 per GPU-hour per 1,000 problems; subscription routes, the tokens they reported at the maker's API list price, nothing billed. Decision and small models were asked one question per request; the subscription models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, MAI) 16 per request through their own tools, marked batched where it matters. The English text was translated from the Turkish originals by Gemini 4 Neon and checked again by GPT-6.2 Astra, every number compared by code. The questions are not published; right or wrong per problem for every run is in https://zekiworks.github.io/analysis/science/answers.json, for paired tests. A reply without a readable letter counts wrong.

rows.normLabel: 0 = no answer right, 100 = every answer right (no options to guess among)
rows.method: ChatGPT subscription (Codex), reasoning high; 16 questions per request; nothing billed
rows.limit: The science bench: hard maths and physics questions, asked in English (the Turkish originals are kept as separate tables at the end of the list). University maths & physics: 50 problems (25 maths, 25 physics) from university textbooks and exams, every given number changed and the answer recomputed by code, five options of which four are typical mistakes. High-school maths: 32 questions from the first stage of a 2026 national high-school maths olympiad, with its official answer key; public since May 2026, so a model trained on later data may have seen them. Broken questions: the 50 university problems mixed with 42 copies in which one given number was changed so that none of the five options is right (checked by code), with a sixth option F 'the question is flawed'; right means F on a broken copy and the right option on an intact one. Exact answers: the same 50 university problems with no options; the model writes the number, right when within 0.1% of the code's value; a reply that is not a number counts wrong. Latency and cost: on our GPU, median seconds per problem with the requests in flight shown, and GPU time from start to last answer × $2.49 per GPU-hour per 1,000 problems; subscription routes, the tokens they reported at the maker's API list price, nothing billed. Decision and small models were asked one question per request; the subscription models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, MAI) 16 per request through their own tools, marked batched where it matters. The English text was translated from the Turkish originals by Gemini 4 Neon and checked again by GPT-6.2 Astra, every number compared by code. The questions are not published; right or wrong per problem for every run is in https://zekiworks.github.io/analysis/science/answers.json, for paired tests. A reply without a readable letter counts wrong.
